scope_classification.in_scope_real_bug: 21 confirmed common-shell bypass forms produce rc=0 in the cooperative-but-buggy threat model. These are NOT adversarial (no subshells, no env-var obfuscation, no eval). A tired cooperative dev WILL type curl --output, wget -P, perl -pi, sudo touch, tar -xC, unzip -d, ln -s -t, pushd, or wrap a write in if/then. The 11-verb-class taxonomy is provably incomplete.
scope_classification.rationale_for_FAIL_not_close_pass: Per dispatch step 4 verbatim: 'If codex finds new bypasses, that's a FAIL.' Per QA Anti-Fraud Principle 5: substituting a related-but-different verification (verifying only the 22 enumerated forms rather than the cooperative-shell completeness the user requested) is forbidden. The user's complaint is about the THREAT MODEL boundary, not about the specific 22 forms. A 22-form whitelist that misses 21 equivalent forms within the same threat model fails the user requirement.

recommendations: Cycle 3 must extend the verb-class taxonomy to cover the 21 confirmed bypass forms. Suggested groupings: (1) curl flag completeness (--output, --output=, -fsSLo), (2) wget -P DIR + ln -s -t DIR + tar -C DIR + unzip -d DIR as a unified 'destination-directory flag' family, (3) in-place mutator family (perl -pi, gawk -i inplace), (4) sudo/env/nice/command/time prefix-stripping pre-pass, (5) pushd/popd in cd-context tracker, (6) cd - rotation handling (track cd-history), (7) if/then/while/for wrapper unwrapping (best-effort via simple sub-command extraction), (8) python -m module + positional-output arg detection, (9) python os.replace/os.rename, (10) node -e fs.writeFileSync, (11) tee --append, (12) >| clobber-redirect, (13) patch + patch -o.
